title: Preservation of finite generators and relations by etale extension
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $c$ a proof-only Zariski-etale module context of [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence], and $F$ a quasi-coherent Zariski module [pqf-def-coherent]. Write $L=c.\mathrm{extension}$ for its canonical tensor extension to small-etale structure modules. If $F$ is of finite type, then $L(F)$ is of finite type. If $F$ is of finite presentation, then $L(F)$ is of finite presentation. These are the site-local finite-generator and finite-relation conditions on the respective sites, without any Noetherian hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 05VG, lemma-equivalence-quasi-coherent-properties, lem-sfb-scheme-etale-module-exact-finiteness-comparison proof step 3: extend Zariski local finite generators and presentations

proof.text: Choose a Zariski open cover carrying a finite generating epimorphism or a finite free presentation. Tensor extension is the left adjoint to restriction, hence preserves epimorphisms and cokernels. The structure-module comparison identifies its finite free terms with the corresponding finite free etale modules.

For each open immersion j:V to T, identify the restricted extension with the extension of j^*F by the tensor-section formula and composition of tensor pullbacks. Etale composition and cancellation identify the slice over V with its small etale site. The open cover is an etale cover, so these finite generators or finite presentations give the asserted site-local property. Empty schemes and zero ranks are allowed.

theorem zariskiEtale_finiteness_preservation (T : Scheme.{u})
    (c : ZariskiEtaleModuleContext T) (F : T.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    (F.IsFiniteType → (c.extension.obj F).IsFiniteType) ∧
      (F.IsFinitePresentation → (c.extension.obj F).IsFinitePresentation)
